parsing_res_list.block_content: At the final steady state ($t \to \infty$), genetic evolution ceases, and $\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}(\infty) = 0$. Substituting Eq. (S23) into this condition yields the total change in genotype:
$$ \begin{aligned}0&=F_{xy}\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}+\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}}\Delta\overline{y}(\infty)\\\Delta\overline{y}(\infty)&=-\frac{F_{xx}F_{xy}}{\det H}\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}\end{aligned} $$
The total long-time change in the phenotype,  $ \Delta\overline{x}_{\text{total}} $, is obtained by evaluating Eq. (S21) at  $ t \to \infty $:

$$ \begin{aligned}\Delta\overline{x}_{total}&=\Delta\overline{x}_{evo}(\infty)+\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}\\&=-\frac{F_{xy}}{F_{xx}}\Delta\overline{y}(\infty)+\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}\\&=\left(1+\frac{F_{xy}^{2}}{\det H}\right)\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}\\ \end{aligned} $$
Because  $ \det H > 0 $, we obtain the inequality  $ |\Delta \overline{x}_{\text{total}}| \geq |\Delta \overline{x}_{\text{plas}}| $.
### S3. EXPONENTIAL DECAY AND MUTATION-SELECTION BALANCE
This section provides the detailed derivations of the exponential relaxation and mutation-selection-balance results presented in the main text.
## Derivation of the evolutionary dynamics and relaxation time

The evolutionary process of the genotype is driven by the Price equation derived in Eq. (S15). Because  $ \overline{y}(0^{+}) $ is constant, we can rewrite  $ \frac{d\overline{y}}{dt} $ as  $ \frac{d}{dt}\Delta\overline{y}(t) $. Substituting the slope at an arbitrary time (Eq. S23) yields:

$$ \begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}\Delta\overline{y}(t)&=G_{yy}\left(F_{xy}\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}+\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}}\Delta\overline{y}(t)\right)\\&=G_{yy}\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}}\Delta\overline{y}(t)+G_{yy}F_{xy}\Delta\overline{x}_{plas}\\&=G_{yy}\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}}\Delta\overline{y}(t)-G_{yy}\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}}\Delta\overline{y}(\infty)\\&=-\frac{1}{\tau}\left(\Delta\overline{y}(t)-\Delta\overline{y}(\infty)\right)\end{aligned} $$

In the third line, we used the steady-state relationship (Eq. S24) to eliminate  $ \Delta \overline{x}_{\text{plas}} $. In the final line, we defined the relaxation time as  $ \tau = -\frac{F_{xx}}{G_{yy} \det H} $.
## Derivation of the steady-state genetic variance
We consider the effective fitness landscape experienced by y when x is optimized. By differentiating the expanded slope (Eq. S23) with respect to  $ \overline{y} $, the effective curvature is:
$$ \frac{\partial^{2}F}{\partial\overline{y}^{2}}=\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}}=-\kappa $$

where  $ \kappa = -\frac{\det H}{F_{xx}} > 0 $. The effective fitness function around the optimal  $ y_{\mathrm{opt}} = \overline{y}(0^{-}) + \Delta \overline{y}(\infty) $ is a quadratic function  $ F(y) = F(y_{\mathrm{opt}}) - \frac{\kappa}{2}(y - y_{\mathrm{opt}})^2 $.

Mapping the continuous-time dynamics to discrete generations, the absolute fitness is  $ \exp(F(y)) $. Selection multiplies the Gaussian distribution  $ P(y) $ (Assumption 4') by a Gaussian weighting factor:
$$ P^{\prime}(y)\propto P(y)\exp\left[-\frac{\kappa}{2}\left(y-y_{opt}\right)^{2}\right] $$
